findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflict checks
findings.body: When an override exists on the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating busy times. An override defines working availability, not permission to ignore existing bookings or external calendar events. Consequently, personal events and fixed or round-robin hosts with an override can expose slots that overlap their existing bookings. Continue to the busy-time checks after validating the override.

findings.title: Override validation checks overlap instead of full slot containment
findings.body: The new override checks reject only slots ending at or before the override start or starting after its end. For a fixed host available from 10:00 to 11:00, a round-robin slot from 09:30 to 10:30 or 10:30 to 11:30 therefore passes, even though the host is unavailable for part of the meeting. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes. Require the entire slot to fit within an override interval.

findings.title: Multiple override intervals reject slots inside a valid interval
findings.body: dateOverrides.find searches for any interval that excludes the slot, rather than an interval that contains it. If a host has overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 on the same date, a 10:00 slot is rejected by the afternoon interval and a 15:00 slot by the morning interval. Split date-override availability can therefore lose all its slots. Group overrides by date and accept containment in any of that date's intervals.

findings.title: Working-hours validation rejects ordinary split schedules
findings.body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working-hours interval on that weekday. For a normal schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, morning slots fail against the afternoon interval and afternoon slots fail against the morning interval. Because every host now goes through this check, this removes valid slots even on dates without overrides. Validate that the full slot is contained in at least one applicable interval instead.

findings.title: Timezone conversion discards midnight rollover
findings.body: The converted override boundaries retain only hour and minute, discarding their date. For example, a UTC override from 22:00 to 23:00 viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30. buildSlots discards that range because start is greater than end, so the valid 23:30–00:30 availability disappears. Converted overrides that cross an attendee's midnight need to be split across the corresponding attendee dates rather than reduced to a single minute-of-day range.
